target: Route "width-amortise" (labels wa:): the amortisation statement that would make thm:qp polynomial; FL(D) at pathwidth three; treewidth one.

findings.defect: CIRCULAR: for each fixed k, PI_k is LOGICALLY EQUIVALENT to the conclusion wa:amortised derives from it, so the route's 'corrected gap' names no statement weaker than its goal. The route asserts the opposite and hands PI_k to a future round as a live question.
findings.evidence: wa:amortised proves PI_k => (stopping payoff games of treewidth <= k in P). The converse is one line, and uses only what wa:amortised itself uses: given H of treewidth <= k, X with |X| <= k+1 and dyadic theta' of bit-size B, the game H[X:=theta'] is stopping (lem:cut-sign), has treewidth <= k (retyping X as terminals deletes X from Gamma, so only edges are lost), and has payoffs of common denominator 2^B*Delta; a polynomial solver for the class returns val, and the greedy pair at val is an optimal positional pair because a stopping game's operator has a unique fixed point (thm:contraction, lem:payoff-transfer(b)) -- verbatim the argument wa:amortised makes at the corner theta = 0. The given pair for H[X:=theta] is simply ignored. Hence PI_k <=> the class-restricted target, and 'answer a query in poly(n) without recursion' = 'solve a treewidth-k game in poly(n)'. The circularity is robust to the obvious weakenings: a query needs only 2(k+1) coordinates of val, but computing val exactly at one named vertex is already the target (prob:main, thm:compare-equivalence); and any H of treewidth <= k occurs as a component C_i of some node of the recursion, so restricting the quantifier to games arising in the recursion restricts nothing. Consequences: (i) the theorem is true but delivers nothing toward an algorithm; (ii) the sharper true statement, which the route does not draw, is that NO amortisation of the shape 'total for all queries = poly(n) x (cost of one query)' can make thm:qp polynomial, since cost-of-one-query is T(n/2) and poly(n)*T(n/2) is n^{Theta(log n)} by the route's own wa:recursion(b) -- so the amortisation paragraph of sec:width should be DELETED as circular, not corrected; (iii) the only non-circular residue is a hypothesis quantified over the query SEQUENCE that thm:tarski actually generates (a chain in the box order, each query determined by the previous response) rather than over all (theta, theta'), and the route does not isolate it. Repair: state it as the paper already states thm:gap-equivalence ('the gap is exactly the problem') -- 'PI_k is exactly prob:main at treewidth k' -- and amend the sentence ALREADY INTEGRATED at frontier.tex:3211 ('the round-16 width route, whose exact statement is a parametric strategy-improvement question'), which currently inherits the route's framing and would send a round after a tautology.

findings.result_name: wa:pi-is-the-pivot (headline: 'the width route lands on the pivot')
findings.defect: False as stated. The route lands on prob:main restricted to treewidth <= k, which is not the pivot; the appeal to cor:selection is rhetorical and does not survive the definition of PI_k.
findings.evidence: The pivot of this document is the all-switches / AUSO identification (prop:allsw-auso, rem:blowup-realise, cor:selection): which improving switch to take on a FIXED game. PI_k as defined is satisfied by any polynomial solver that performs no switch at all (see the fatal finding), so it is not 'cor:selection's selection problem in parametric form'. thm:short-path says only that SOME sequence of <= |Vmax| switches connects the two pairs; it does not make a statement whose truth is equivalent to a poly-time solver into a selection statement. The remark's own hedge ('weaker than "strategy improvement is polynomial at treewidth k" in one direction only') is true but conceals the informative fact, that PI_k is equivalent to the class being in P.

findings.defect: Rediscovers, unlabelled, a disclaimer the paper already prints; and the measurement is taken on instances the paper itself classifies as never hard to solve, so it cannot bear on PI_k. Presented as a Proposition.
findings.evidence: (a) rem:fold (frontier.tex l.12599) already says: 'It does not rule out parametric methods that avoid tracking the pair, and we claim nothing about those.' wa:warm-measured's conclusion ('rem:fold-width says nothing against PI_k') is that sentence, restated with numbers and without citation. (b) P_D and FL(D) are in K_1 of thm:bounded-components: their Max vertices F_d reach only F_{d-1}, so H(G) is acyclic and all-switches halts within |Vmax| rounds COLD. Measuring warm-start savings there measures nothing. (c) The route's own logs contradict the emphasis: logs/warm_PD.txt and warm_FL.txt give cold-max = warm-max = D-1 at EVERY D (the warm start does not reduce the per-query maximum at all), and the totals are 48 cold vs 36 warm at D = 9, a 1.3x saving; the warm totals are exactly the triangular numbers D(D-1)/2, i.e. Theta(D) rounds per query, not O(1). The headline ratios 4.5-2390 are on random games only, and the logs stop at D = 9 (P_D) and D = 8 (FL) while the LaTeX reports D = 2..12. The concluding sentence 'the piece count is exponential exactly where the warm start is cheap' is true only because cold is cheap there too.

findings.defect: The asserted law ('the counts jump with the depth exactly as wa:recursion predicts') is contradicted by the route's own logs, and the LaTeX remark quotes a selected subset of the rows.
findings.evidence: logs/mm_k2.log, depth is recorded per size: n=16 is depth 1 with 124.2 queries while n=20 is depth 2 with 84.0 -- fewer queries at greater depth; the depth-2 row sequence is 84.0, 147639.2, 1060.5, 135405.8, 29504.2, 3106.2, non-monotone by three orders of magnitude. logs/mm_k3.log depth-2 rows: 6612, 2709, 1012, 14778, 97627, 1019229 -- likewise. Worse, mm_k3 at n=40 records 1,019,229.5 queries against only 29,008.5 recursive solves, i.e. FEWER solves than queries, which contradicts the report's own cost model ('each query costs one recursive solve in every component') and is unexplained. Four trials per size cannot support a law. The LaTeX remark quotes k=2 n=12 (27.5) against k=2 n=24 (147639) and omits n=16, 20, 28, 32, 36, 40.

findings.defect: Standard published mathematics presented without acknowledgement, and the paper's own proof of thm:qp already performs the same unrolling; only one of the readings of the ambiguous sentence is refuted.
findings.evidence: (a) is the textbook substitution-method master theorem for T(n) <= Q sum_i T(n_i) + p(n) with sum n_i <= n and n_i <= n/2 (Bentley-Haken-Saxe / Akra-Bazzi lineage; from memory, unchecked); (b) is the standard unrolling that turns a per-level factor n^c into n^{Theta(c log n)}. Neither is attributed, against the round's rule 6. The paper already displays the same computation inside the proof of thm:qp: 'T(n) <= n^{O(k)} . n T(n/2) + poly and T(n) <= (n^{O(k)})^{log_2 n} = 2^{O(k log^2 n)}', and the paragraph after thm:qp already states the mechanism ('the recursion re-solves both sides from scratch at every query, so the query cost is raised to the depth'). Separately, under the other natural reading of 'polynomially related' (total <= p(single) with deg p = c > 1) the recursion gives T(n) <= T(n/2)^c, i.e. 2^{n^{log_2 c}} -- worse than the route's n^{Theta(log n)}; the route refutes only the multiplicative-factor reading. The residual value is editorial (the paper's gap sentence was ambiguous) and has already been integrated at frontier.tex l.3203-3211.

findings.defect: The only clause of wa:forest-poly not already implied by wa:forest-k1 + thm:bounded-components is 'No stopping hypothesis is needed', and it is precisely the clause the route's own scripts never tested.
findings.evidence: wa/t_forest2.py and wa/t_forest3.py both contain 'if not isf or not is_stopping(g): skipped += 1; continue', and logs/forest_large.txt reports non-stopping = 45, 55, 66, 76, 80, 80 SKIPPED at n = 20..160. So the ~400 verified games are all stopping, where wa:forest-k1 already puts the game in K_1 and thm:bounded-components already gives polynomial time. I tested the missing clause myself (audit-wa/nonstop.py): 8563 NON-stopping random forest games with self-loops over three seeds (n <= 10), forest.solve_forest against an exact reference max_sigma min_tau Pr[reach t1] computed as a least fixed point (zero on the no-escape set, exact Gaussian elimination elsewhere) -- 0 disagreements. The clause holds, and I checked the proof's lfp cases (self-loop at Max gives max(theta,0) = theta, at Min gives min(theta,0) = 0, at avg gives theta) by hand. But the route reported as checked something it had filtered out. Also note the class is vanishingly thin: at n = 120 and n = 160 the route's generator produced ZERO stopping forest games in 80 tries.

findings.defect: FL(D) is defined only as a payoff game: the vertex u is never given a kind or out-edges, yet |V| = D^2+4D+3 counts it.
findings.evidence: def wa:def-fl lists X_d, Y_d, F_d, G_d, C_{d,j} and sets 'F_0 := u', but u appears only as the frozen parameter. thm:fold's P_D is explicit (u in Vavg, u -> (t0,t1)); FL(D) needs the same sentence to be an SSG under def:ssg (out-degree exactly two) rather than a payoff game with a parameter terminal. My verification (audit-wa/fl.py) treated u as a terminal, as the route's own code does.

findings.defect: Verified correct and genuinely new to the paper, but small: it trades rem:fold-width's 2^{Omega(N)} for 2^{Omega(sqrt N)} to buy one unit of width, and closes a question the paper explicitly calls immaterial.
findings.evidence: I re-derived it independently (audit-wa/fl.py, widthlib.py): the closed form 2^{-(D+1)}(theta + 1 - 2^{-D} + 2^{-D} T^D(theta)) checked at 11 rationals (1/3, 2/7, 5/11, 1/2, 3/4, 17/64, 9/32, 100/257, 0, 1, 7/16) for D = 1..4 against BRUTE-FORCE max-min over all positional pairs (not policy iteration), 0 mismatches; stopping by the trap characterisation; |V| = D^2+4D+3 confirmed; the stated path decomposition verified bag-by-bag (all bags <= 4, every edge covered, every vertex contiguous) for D <= 9; the K_4 minor {X_1,F_1,X_2}, {G_1,Y_2}, {F_2,X_3,F_3,Y_3}, {G_2} verified disjoint, connected and pairwise adjacent for 3 <= D <= 9. So tw = pw = 3 for D >= 3. FL(D) is P_D with the shared constant chain replaced by pendant chains -- a one-idea variation, which the route says plainly. rem:fold-width's own text says 'nothing in this document depends on the answer', and its working conclusion ('every dynamic programme that stores them is exponential') is already delivered by the pathwidth-four statement.

findings.defect: FL(D) and P_D are both in K_1 of thm:bounded-components, so neither is a hardness family; this should be said when 2^{Omega(sqrt N)} is printed.
findings.evidence: In FL(D), F_d's successors X_d, Y_d lead only to level d-1, so H(FL(D)) is acyclic on F_1..F_D and every strongly connected component is a singleton: FL(D) is in K_1 and all-switches halts within |Vmax| rounds. Same for P_D. This matches the paragraph after thm:qp ('they were never hard to solve') and is exactly why wa:warm-measured's measurement on these families carries no information.

findings.defect: Correct, honestly negative, and the route's own next_steps concede the point: no seventh polynomial class is claimed, and none exists here.
findings.evidence: I verified the proof (the unique Gamma-path between two mutually reachable controlled vertices is forced to be a trap, contradicting lem:trapchar via out-degree two) and the sharpness witness by exact computation: x -> (m,t0) Max, m -> (y,t1) avg, y -> (q,t0) Max, q -> (x,t0) avg is stopping, Gamma is a 4-cycle (tw 2), val = (2/3, 2/3, 1/3, 1/3), and x, y are mutually reachable -- so the witness is in K_2, still inside thm:bounded-components. Treewidth 1 is inside K_1; thm:qp's class is quasipolynomial and so is not a polynomial class at all. The route says both. wa:tw2-open is correspondingly thin: logs/tp_k2.log rests on 3 games at n = 30 and 12 at n = 26, and the route labels it as not evidence.

verdict: MIXED -- integrating the whole route would make the paper WORSE; integrating two of its seven results would make it BETTER. Novelty: nothing here restates thm:ladder, thm:short-path, lem:cut, lem:duality, thm:seed-dichotomy, lem:rise-bound or thm:bsi-tracks. Two unlabelled rediscoveries: wa:recursion is the textbook master-theorem substitution plus the standard n^c-per-level unrolling (and the paper's own thm:qp proof already displays it); wa:warm-measured's conclusion is rem:fold's own printed disclaimer at l.12599. INTEGRATE: (1) wa:fold3 and a trimmed wa:fold3-checked, replacing rem:fold-width's sentence 'Whether the explosion already occurs at pathwidth three is open' -- I re-derived the closed form, the stopping property, the width-3 path decomposition and the K_4 minor independently and all hold; add one clause saying FL(D) is in K_1 and hence not a hardness family, and give u a kind and out-edges. (2) wa:forest-k1 with its treewidth-2 witness, as a one-paragraph negative closing the seventh-class hope at treewidth one; keep 'the branch response has at most two affine pieces' as a sentence inside it rather than as wa:forest-response + wa:forest-poly as theorems, since for stopping games the polynomial-time conclusion is thm:bounded-components and the only novel clause (no stopping hypothesis) was untested by the route -- I tested it and it holds, so it may be stated, attributed to this audit's check. DO NOT INTEGRATE: wa:warm-measured (a Proposition whose conclusion is already in rem:fold and whose data are taken on K_1 instances where cold is cheap too); wa:qp-measured as a remark asserting a law (the logs contradict it; keep at most one sentence that thm:qp was implemented, run to completion and cross-checked against Hoffman-Karp); wa:tw2-open beyond half a sentence. INTEGRATE ONLY AFTER RELABELLING: wa:pi + wa:amortised. Its hypothesis PI_k is equivalent, for each fixed k, to its conclusion, by a one-line converse the route missed, so it is not a gap and must not be offered as one. It belongs in the paper the way thm:gap-equivalence does -- 'PI_k is exactly prob:main at treewidth k' -- together with the sharper corollary the route stopped short of: no amortisation of the form 'total for all queries = poly(n) x cost of one query' can make thm:qp polynomial, because cost-of-one-query is T(n/2) and wa:recursion(b) turns any such factor into n^{Theta(log n)}; hence the amortisation paragraph of sec:width should be DELETED as circular rather than corrected. THE ROUTE'S REAL REMAINING GAP, more precisely than the route states it: there is none of the strength the route claims -- the only shape of amortisation that is not immediately equivalent to solving the class is one quantified over the query SEQUENCE thm:tarski actually generates at a node (a chain in the box order, each query determined by the previous response) rather than over all pairs (theta, theta'), namely: 'for each fixed k there is a polynomial q such that, for every stopping payoff game of treewidth <= k, every separator node of the recursion, and the specific chain theta_1, ..., theta_L of at most O(B^{k+1}) query vectors the thm:tarski search visits there, the responses at theta_2, ..., theta_L are computed in total time q(n+B) from the response at theta_1' -- and that statement is neither proved, refuted, nor stated by the route. ACTION ITEM ON THE LIVE FILE: the amortisation paragraph at frontier.tex l.3203-3211 has already been edited this round to carry the route's framing ('the round-16 width route, whose exact statement is a parametric strategy-improvement question'); that clause is the circular one and should say instead that the statement is equivalent to prob:main restricted to treewidth k.
